draft.title: Medicines from plants
card: An active ingredient is the chemical in a plant that has a medical effect. Chemists first take it out of the plant material, then purify it.

plant material is mixed with a solvent that dissolves the wanted compound better than it dissolves the rest. The solution is then separated from the solid plant matter. Polar compounds dissolve best in polar solvents, and non-polar compounds in non-polar solvents.

a mixture of liquids is heated and the parts boil off at different temperatures. The vapour of the part with the lower boiling point is cooled and collected first. This separates the extracted compound from the solvent or from other liquids.
Extraction gives a mixture, so a further purifying step is usually needed. Testing then shows whether the purified compound has a medical effect.
draft.remember: Extraction takes a compound out of a plant using a solvent. Distillation purifies it by boiling point.

a.q: Why is distillation used after solvent extraction of a plant?
opts: To separate liquids in the mixture by boiling point
To make the plant material dissolve in the solvent
To separate liquids in the mixture by their polarity
To make the solvent boil at the same temperature
a.why: Extraction gives a mixture of dissolved compounds and solvent. Distillation separates the liquids because they boil at different temperatures. Polarity is what decides how well a compound dissolves during extraction, not how it is separated in distillation.
a.clue: Think about what differs between the liquids as they are heated.

b.q: Mia wants to extract a non-polar compound from crushed leaves. Which solvent should she choose, and why?
opts: A non-polar solvent, as it dissolves the compound better
A polar solvent, as it dissolves the compound better
A non-polar solvent, as it has a higher boiling point
A polar solvent, as it has a lower boiling point
b.why: A non-polar compound dissolves best in a non-polar solvent, so this solvent takes it out of the leaves. A polar solvent would dissolve the compound poorly. Boiling point matters for distillation later, not for choosing how well the solvent extracts.
b.clue: Which solvent dissolves the compound best?

a.best: To separate liquids in the mixture by boiling point

b.best: A non-polar solvent, as it dissolves the compound better
